QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_14

question.text: Hampi Capital seeks 75% LP approval for in-specie distribution of an unliquidated IT-services investment. SEBI's April-2024 circular requires the manager to arrange a BID for the asset of at least:

answer.text: 10% of the value of unliquidated investments, to fund dissenters
25% of the value of unliquidated investments, for dissenter and pro-rata exits
50% of the value of unliquidated investments, for optional exits
100% of the value, since a cash exit must be fully available

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI Circular 26-Apr-2024 requires the AIF to arrange bids for a MINIMUM of 25% of the value of unliquidated investments. Dissenters get first priority to exit from this 25% tranche; any unsubscribed portion is offered pro-rata to non-dissenting investors. If the manager fails to arrange the 25% bid, the in-specie distribution is recorded at INR 1 for track-record purposes. The Trap: 10% / 50% / 100% are distractors; 25% is the precise regulatory threshold. Cross-Exam Context: Pure XIX-C content; Distributor exams do not test this operational detail. Manager's Pro-Tip: Line up the 25% bidder BEFORE calling the LP vote — a 'bid-conditional' vote collapses if the bidder walks, and you lose LP credibility. Use a reputable secondary buyer and share the term sheet with the LPAC upfront.
